cards.style_profile: Durable high-volume rhythm distributor: wins with timing, quick release and ball security from the pocket (3.5% sack rate, 0 fumbles), short-area heavy (aDOT 7.8, 8.2% deep); limited intermediate/deep accuracy and little legs value — distinct from Burrow's precision and Jackson's improvisation.
Gridiron Standard. Backup quarterback with no 2026 grade on the public Cowboys table. The 2023 Washington season is the last full body of work.
Gridiron Standard. Between-the-tackles lead back. The 2026 grade is solid, not a home-run profile.
Gridiron Standard. Smaller change-of-pace back on a short 2026 sample.

Hunter Luepke: Athletic, multi-use fullback: 16-71 rushing and 13-109 receiving (2025, most touches of any true FB), PFF 60.5 on 252 snaps then 54.5 on 95; explosive and quick, a ball-handling FB whose blocking is solid but not dominant.

CeeDee Lamb: Movable three-level volume WR: most targets in football (94), TPRR .318, PFF 89.7 after a 77.6 dip in 2025; strong route breaks and deep EPA (+1.16), with average contested and tackle-breaking ability.

George Pickens: Highlight-catch boundary threat: 1,429 yds and EPA/target +.64 in 2025 with the best spectacular-catch profile; 2026 dropped (PFF 78.1, YPRR 1.72, deep catch 33%), and his route discipline and focus are inconsistent.
Gridiron Standard. Starting third receiver whose 2026 grade fell off the 2025 mark.
Gridiron Standard. Small return specialist. The public PFF row has no 40 time, so speed is not a 90.
Gridiron Standard. Big reserve receiver with a modest grade and a cited 4.46.
Gridiron Standard. Rookie with one counted 2026 snap. The grade is not a season.
Gridiron Standard. Listed starting tight end with a poor 2026 grade on a real snap count.
Gridiron Standard. Larger inline tight end. His 2026 grade is ahead of the listed starter.
Gridiron Standard. Third tight end. The table cites a 4.63 forty and a modest grade.
Gridiron Standard. Young left tackle. The 2026 grade improved on 2025 and is still short of a top-10 tackle.
Gridiron Standard. Rookie tackle on five 2026 snaps. The 39.4 grade is not treated as a full season.
Tyler Smith: Explosive physical freak: biggest power profile at guard but PFF 73.4/71.9 and 7 accepted penalties in 2025 (worst in the pool); only 4 games in 2026.
Gridiron Standard. Swing interior lineman. The table cites a 5.48 forty, so he is not a phone-booth-only guard.
Cooper Beebe: Thick converted-guard anchor: ESPN IOL PBWR 92%, 1 penalty in two seasons, PFF 67.8 / 69.1; stout vs power but limited range and 11 games in 2025.

Tyler Booker: Young power mauler on the rise: PFF 72.0 as a 2025 rookie then 83.1 (#6 G) in 2026 at age 22.5; road-grader strength and a firm anchor, but 9 penalties in two seasons (5 holdings, 3 unnecessary roughness) and an ankle that cost three 2025 games.
Gridiron Standard. Second right guard with no 2026 row on the public PFF table.
Gridiron Standard. Starting right tackle on a down 2026 grade after a fuller snap count.
Gridiron Standard. Former first-round tackle on a 36-snap 2026 sample. Draft slot is not the rating.
Gridiron Standard. Every-down edge on a down 2026 grade. ESPN lists him at weak-side linebacker; that is the chart side, not a tracked snap study.
Gridiron Standard. Older edge whose 2026 grade is good on 121 snaps. Age and sample keep him out of the 80s.
Gridiron Standard. Situational rusher. The 2026 sample is 33 snaps.
Gridiron Standard. Young edge starter. 2026 is below his 2025 grade. ESPN strong-side linebacker is the chart side used for REDGE.
Gridiron Standard. Rookie edge with a low grade on 226 snaps. The first-round tag is not the rating.
Gridiron Standard. Edge depth on 21 snaps. A 4.65 forty is on the 2026 table.
Quinnen Williams: Explosive gap-shooter: PFF 88.7 (2025), 26 pressures, 21 TFL across 2025-26 and ESPN RSWR 38% (#9 DT); best first step in the group, but PFF fell to 67.2 at DAL in 2026.
Gridiron Standard. Heavy interior starter. His 2026 grade is ahead of the other non-locked tackles.
Gridiron Standard. Veteran interior tackle whose 2026 grade is ordinary on a full snap load.
Gridiron Standard. Reserve interior tackle on a short snap count.
Gridiron Standard. Listed mike whose 2026 sample is short and graded lower than 2025. A 4.56 forty is on the 2025 table.
Gridiron Standard. Second-level linebacker coming off a poor 2025 grade and an ordinary 2026.
Gridiron Standard. Smaller will linebacker. The 2025 table cites a 4.49 forty.
Gridiron Standard. Rookie linebacker with more 2026 snaps than the listed mike and a slightly higher grade.
Gridiron Standard. Long corner on a partial 2026 snap count. A 4.46 forty is on the table.
Gridiron Standard. Listed starter whose 2026 grade collapsed on 539 snaps. Current season leads the prior year.
Gridiron Standard. Rookie safety playing the nickel on the ESPN chart. Rated at CB for that published role, not as a deep safety.
Gridiron Standard. Smaller corner on a partial snap count and a middling grade.
Gridiron Standard. Tall corner with poor grades in both retrieved seasons.
Gridiron Standard. Reserve corner around a 50 grade.
Gridiron Standard. Veteran free safety. The card is FS because ESPN lists him there; the registry bucket was SS.
Gridiron Standard. Young safety on 83 snaps.
Gridiron Standard. Listed strong safety after a poor grade on 99 snaps. The starter tag does not repair the grade.
Gridiron Standard. Box safety. 2026 is better than 2025 and still not a starter grade.
Gridiron Standard. Third safety. The 2026 grade is 20 snaps.
Brandon Aubrey: Elite leg, recent wobble: PFF 94.0 (K rank 1, 2025) with 4 of 8 from 60+ and a 64-yard long over 2025-26, but 2026 FG EPA just +0.8 with 2 blocked.
Bryan Anger: Veteran placement punter: 0 touchbacks in 60 punts, 57.9% inside-20 in 2026, net 42.6 / 42.5.
Trent Sieg: Strong 2025: unit points 15.8 with 0 blocks; 2026 unit points -1.3 with 2 blocks.
